request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows a "Watched due total" for whoever is signed in, and all 4 acceptance tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

It adds up the due-totals of the people that user watches and shows 0.00 when they watch no one. Each user sees their own total: in the test, uma and vic watch different people on the same sheet and get different figures.

The change is only in `src/main/frontend/features/header/header.slot.tsx`. The server already sends each user's watched list and every person's due-total, so it needed no changes, and nothing new is written to the audit file.

Two details of how the sum works:
- **No trimming:** the sheet's own due total drops the highest and lowest figure. The watched total doesn't; it is a straight sum, like the existing crew total.
- **"n/a" is skipped:** a watched person whose due-total is "n/a" is left out of the sum.
